source.title: Audio--Image Alignment as a Continued-Pretraining Stage in Automatic Speech Recognition
source.authors: Sujith Pulikodan; Nihar Desai; Prasanta Kumar Ghosh

record.tranche_reason: The study deliberately trains an audio encoder to align with image embeddings as a method for improving ASR, and reports downstream ASR and retrieval performance. It does not test whether alignment arises or increases naturally with model scale or capability.
record.gate_note: The reported audio-to-image and image-to-audio retrieval scores directly measure retrieval by intentionally aligned models, so they are recorded under fits_no_version rather than as evidence for natural convergence or interchangeability. The FLEURS WER comparisons, shuffled-pair control, and fine-tuning-budget results measure downstream ASR performance, not convergence between independently trained representations, and are not rows for these claim versions. The authors' alignment training deliberately induces the alignment.
record.test_reason: The study contrastively trains a FastConformer audio encoder to match frozen image-encoder embeddings as an ASR adaptation step. It reports WER and retrieval of its own method only. It never measures alignment arising between independently trained models, so no version is tested. It also does not cite the originals; T6 would be defensible.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors find the three image encoders give nearly equal ASR gains (<0.4 WER points) and that retrieval quality does not predict ASR gain. They interpret alignment as a semantic regulariser on the encoder.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a FastConformer audio encoder with a contrastive audio–image alignment stage for ASR adaptation; it does not reproduce a method for testing naturally emerging representational convergence.
record.method_sensitivity: Retrieval scores vary across the three image-encoder/alignment configurations and between audio-to-image and image-to-audio retrieval.

fits_no_version.finding: After contrastive training, all three configurations reach held-out audio–image retrieval R@1 of 0.09–0.17 in both directions, against chance of 0.00026.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Contrastively aligning a speech encoder to frozen image embeddings yields above-chance audio–image retrieval.

fits_no_version.finding: With the trained-alignment setup, the largest image encoders (SigLIP2 Large at about 303M, Qwen3-VL at about 500M) retrieve worse than SigLIP2 Base (about 86M). Retrieval quality does not predict ASR gain.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In trained audio–image alignment, a larger vision backbone does not increase achieved cross-modal alignment.

record.problems: The retrieval evaluation is on held-out data from the study's alignment setup and measures performance after alignment was deliberately trained; it does not compare independently trained models across scale or capability. Retrieval uncertainty is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: Downstream ASR WER results, including FLEURS comparisons, the shuffled-pair control, and fine-tuning-duration results, are not rows because they measure ASR outcomes rather than representational convergence or retrieval.

untested.parts: All: no independently trained models are compared across scale.
All: no natural vision–language alignment is measured; alignment is trained audio–image.
All: no post-hoc mapping or stitching of independent models. The trained projection is a full contrastive fine-tune, not a simple map.
All: no feature or circuit analysis.
All: no analysis of natural alignment level or its causes.

record.verdict_notes: The study deliberately induces alignment, which the verdict rules exclude from testing. Consider moving the tranche to T6, since the study does not cite the PRH or convergent-learning originals.

versions.untested_parts: Whether independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data become more aligned as size or capability increases.
Whether vision and language models' representations of paired images and captions align more as both models improve; this study uses audio and images and trains alignment deliberately.
Whether different initialization seeds of the same architecture learn shared features or subspaces.
Whether representations are interchangeable with little loss through simple mappings, stitching, relative representations, or without paired data.
Whether interpretable features or circuits recur across models.
Whether convergence results depend on similarity metrics, settings, or input distributions.
Whether alignment remains incomplete or plateaus, and whether shared data or objectives explain it.

rows.stage_stated: audio–image alignment, followed by ASR fine-tuning
rows.operation_detail: Held-out audio-to-image retrieval evaluation after audio–image alignment training
rows.note: Retrieval is evaluated after alignment was intentionally trained; this is not a test of alignment emerging with scale or capability.
rows.check: Retrieval after deliberately trained alignment measures the study's own method, not natural convergence. Keep as a fits_no_version row; 'observed' against chance is not a claim-version state.
